questions.question: In affine coordinates on a twisted Edwards curve, what point acts as the identity element?
questions.explanation: For Edwards/twisted Edwards curves the neutral element is the ordinary affine point (0,1), not a special point at infinity.

questions.question: In Ed25519 compressed point encoding, what information is stored directly in the 32-byte string?
options: The y-coordinate plus one x bit
The x-coordinate plus one y bit
questions.explanation: Ed25519 encodes y (255 bits, little-endian) and one sign bit for x.

questions.question: Why do extended Edwards coordinates speed up point addition and doubling compared to affine formulas?
options: They avoid using the curve equation
They avoid tracking any Z coordinate
questions.explanation: Extended/projective-style coordinates replace division by Z with extra multiplications, avoiding expensive modular inversions in the main loop.

questions.question: For Edwards25519, what is the curve cofactor (the small factor multiplying the large prime subgroup order)?
questions.explanation: Edwards25519 has group order 8·l, so the cofactor is 8.

questions.question: What does a prime-subgroup membership check for Edwards25519 typically verify?
options: It checks that l·P equals the identity
It checks that 8·P equals the identity
It checks that P has x equal to zero
It checks that y is below p
questions.explanation: Being in the prime-order subgroup of size l means multiplying by l yields the identity element.

questions.question: If a protocol computes shared = secret·P on Edwards25519 with attacker-chosen P, which attacker choice best enables a small-subgroup confinement attack?
options: Any point with even y value
questions.explanation: A torsion point of order 2/4/8 forces the result into a tiny set, leaking secret modulo that small order.

questions.question: Which mitigation most directly prevents small-subgroup confinement when using attacker-supplied Edwards25519 points in scalar multiplication?
options: Reject points not in the l subgroup
Use a shorter secret scalar value
Encode the point as base64 first
questions.explanation: Subgroup validation (l·P = identity) or an equivalent defense ensures the attacker cannot force computations into the small torsion subgroup.

questions.question: What does clearing the cofactor on Edwards25519 mean in practice for a point P?
options: Replace P with l·P before use
Replace P with P plus the identity
Replace P with the basepoint B
questions.explanation: Multiplying by the cofactor (8) maps any on-curve point into the prime-order subgroup, removing the torsion component.
